title: `post-stamped` refuses a `{{WAS:}}`-declared stamp inside a fenced code block, and its refusal prescribes the declaration that is already there
body:
## What was measured

Measured by the `domain:spec` seat at 2026-09-20T11:05Z while writing a landing record, on the `scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs` that is on `origin/main` at `e3b3cdd2df3`. Reproduced three times in a row; the fix that worked is at the bottom.

A body carried `{{NOW}}` twice, and a quoted stamp inside a **fenced code block** — a pasted `git log` line — declared exactly as the contract prescribes:

    ```
    44a23329f70a9087298726157f984ae9573b62ee  {{WAS:2026-09-20T10:25:40Z}}
    fix(spec): `undoable` names the written set, not `patch` alone (#19283)
    ```

`post-stamped --comment=19148` **refused it**, exit 2, nothing written:

> 1. [mixed] this body uses `{{NOW}}` and also carries the bare stamp `2026-09-20T10:25:40Z`. One of the two clocks was read by this act and the other was typed; a reader cannot tell which. Declare it with `{{WAS:2026-09-20T10:25:40Z}}` **if it is a quoted reading**, or make it `{{NOW}}` if it is this act's own.

⭐ The remedy the refusal names was **already applied**, character for character, at the position it is complaining about. The two readers disagree:

- the **MIXED scan** reads the text inside a fenced block, sees `2026-09-20T10:25:40Z`, and files it as bare;
- the **declaration reader** does not count a `{{WAS:…}}` opener inside that same fence — consistent with the tool's own summary line, which reports `verbatim: 0 opener(s) inside a quoted span, left exactly as written (none)` on the successful run.

⇒ **a correctly declared quoted stamp inside a fenced code block is unpostable**, and the refusal text sends the author in a circle.

## The controlled fix

Moving the identical stamp out of the fence, declared identically, posted first try:

```
exit=0
post-stamped: comment posted on objectstack-ai/objectstack#19148
  comment: 5749403654
  substitutions: 2 {{NOW}}, 9 quoted · verbatim: 0 opener(s) inside a quoted span, left exactly as written (none)
```

⇒ the discriminator is the fence, ⛔ not the stamp, not the seconds grain, and not the `{{NOW}}` count. Control: the same body's eight other `{{WAS:…}}` stamps, all outside fences, were accepted throughout all three refusals.

## Why it is worth a line rather than a shrug

Pasting a `git log` line, a gate's output or an API reading into a fenced block is what a landing record, a verdict and a round report all do — and those readings carry stamps by construction, because 「板面/树/队列读数恒带 UTC 取数时刻」. So this cell is on the path of the artefacts the stamp contract exists to protect, and the workaround (restructure the prose so no quoted stamp sits in a fence) is discoverable only by hitting the refusal and disbelieving it.

⛔ This is ⛔ **not** a request to weaken the contract. Three arms look defensible and this seat picks none of them: teach the declaration reader to see `{{WAS:…}}` inside a fence; or exempt fenced content from the MIXED scan the way it is already exempt from substitution; or keep the behaviour and make the refusal say so, naming the fence and the remedy. The third is a one-line change to the refusal text.

## Dedup words

`post-stamped`, `{{WAS:}}`, `mixed`, `fenced code block`, `stamp contract`

Origin: measured in the act of writing the #19148 landing record (comment 5749403654). Filed-by: `session_01LvwGppdonww4zGLWZo5rho` (`domain:spec` execution seat 1) — a platform-fact finding routed to the `skills` lane per 「平台事实变化 → references 事实表改一行」; ⛔ not graded or routed by this seat.
